prompt:
I need the front end for Airshift. A messaging tool for volunteer-run community radio stations, where the volunteer coordinator, show hosts, engineers and board members talk through shift swaps, on-air incidents and station business over days and weeks.

Who's using it: Dev Raman, the unpaid volunteer coordinator at KRVT 92.7, a low-power FM community station in a small river town, run entirely by about 45 volunteers on a budget of roughly $18,000 a year. Dev works days as a pharmacy tech and handles station messages at night and on lunch breaks.

What they're doing right now: Last Thursday the 'Night Market' world-music show went to dead air for 11 minutes, and a listener emailed the station complaining. Dev is now juggling several conversations about it: he has to ask the host, Lourdes, what happened without sounding accusatory, check with the volunteer engineer, Walt, whether the automation fallback failed, and reply to the listener. In the same evening he also has to find someone to cover Saturday's 6–8 a.m. farm report, since its host messaged that she's sick, and answer a new volunteer who's been waiting four days to hear about board-op training.

What's in the system at this point: 45 volunteers, each with role (host, board op, engineer, board member, trainee) and the shows they're tied to; 23 weekly shows. Conversations: 1:1 thread with Lourdes Ibarra (last message 3 days ago, 'Sorry about Thursday—can we talk?'); thread with Walt Shumaker including a log excerpt ('automation failover: no response 21:42–21:53'); group conversation 'Weekend hosts' with 14 members, 6 unread; the listener email from 'm.halvorsen@…' forwarded into the station inbox; message from Joy Carter, 'Farm Report', sent 2 hours ago, 'flu, can't do Sat'; trainee Abel Nguyen's message from Nov 12 still unanswered; board thread 'Spring pledge drive' with 31 messages since October. Dev has saved replies for common things (training sign-up, swap etiquette). 3 hosts have said they're willing to fill in on early-morning slots.

Build it as a working web app, opened in the state that person would see at that moment. No backend: use realistic mock data (no lorem ipsum, no placeholder names), and make the interactive parts actually work client-side.

Use whatever framework and tooling you like. When you're done there must be a static production build in ./out with ./out/index.html as the entry point. It will be served from the root of a plain static file server (no rewrites, no server code) and viewed in a desktop browser at 1440×900.
